headline: Reduced physical models of single-cell confinement, chirality and state transitions
label: Biophysical Models Of Cell Mechanics
summary: Preprints now pair confinement, stochastic landscapes and parameter-sensitivity analysis with single-cell state dynamics in reduced models.
synthesis: The three preprints share a reduced-model approach to single-cell dynamics, in which effective equations or low-dimensional formulations are derived and tested against a defined system. A cellular phase-field model relates confinement strength to chiral rotation regimes and is validated on MCF10A cells in Matrigel. A second preprint applies Fisher information to single-cell state transitions, reporting sloppy parameter structure and approximate least-action paths. The third extends dynamical mean field theory to gene regulatory networks with slow epigenetic feedback variables, yielding effective stochastic equations; it addresses regulatory rather than mechanical dynamics. What is new across the set is the pairing of geometric or mechanical constraint with statistical-inference and stochastic-landscape descriptions of cell-state behavior, rather than any single method.
